data.note:
Mistake: blinded conclusion Microtubule stabilizers was wrong; true MoA Actin disruptors (cytochalasin B).

What misled me: monotonic tub_mean to z+44.6 and bundling language at 3uM (e15) plus stabilizer neighbours in combined atlas (e5). Literature supports actin-filament capping/disruption framing for cytochalasin B vs latrunculin comparison: PMID:8781335; actin filament assembly/capping biology: PMID:1608453, PMID:12686620.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth was cytochalasin B, an Actin disruptor; I twice concluded Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.62 then p=0.38 and was wrong. The central error was treating monotonic tub_mean brightening to z=+44.6 at 30uM (e3) with rho=+1.00 (e9) and multinucleation to z~+21 at 3uM (e8) as stabilizer-specific.

The actin signal was present from the start but I discounted it. The 30uM microscopist read was Actin disruptors with no distinct bundles (e4), low doses already showed cell_area z=-8.4 to -4.1 with multinucleation z=+8.4 to +3.4 (e2, e7), and act_mean also rose with rho=+1.00 to z=+37.3 (e11). That pattern fits actin filament capping and failed cytokinesis rather than stabilization, consistent with cytochalasin B as a microfilament-disrupting agent (PMID 8781335) acting by barbed-end capping (PMID 12686620, PMID 10340699), where loss of directed assembly collapses morphology (PMID 1608453).

I was misled by acquisition and weighting choices: only n=1 per dose over 4 wells, so dose-responses were four single wells; high-dose rounding/compaction inflated tub and actin texture (tub_glcm_contrast z=+44.1, act_glcm_contrast z=+67.5 in e3); and I over-weighted one bundle-like vision at 3uM (e15) over conflicting visions (e4, e19) and atlas neighbours that never supported stabilizers at 1uM and 3uM — Protein synthesis 8/10 (e13) and Epithelial 5/10 (e18). The review was correct that actin was not shown to be secondary.

e2/e7/e8 cell_area shrinkage with reduced density and rising frac_multinucleate_proxy captured cytokinesis failure from actin-ring disruption
e11 act_mean rho=+1.00 to high z and e3 actin texture explosion showed actin was co-primary, not secondary
e13/e14/e18 atlas neighbours (Protein synthesis 8/10, Cholesterol-lowering 5/10, Epithelial 5/10) correctly warned against stabilizers
what_was_wrong: misread tub_mean rise to z=+44.6 (e3, e8, e9) as stabilization when actin-collapse compaction also brightens tubulin
treated multinucleation (e2, e8, e10) as stabilizer/Aurora-specific and missed actin-cytokinesis failure
upgraded single 3uM bundle-like vision (e15) and initial atlas 3/10 stabilizers (e5) to p=0.62 despite e4 contradiction and n=1/dose
failed to resolve that tub_mean and act_mean both had rho=+1.00 (e9 vs e11), so specificity for stabilizers was never demonstrated

citations.claim: Cytochalasin B is a microfilament-disrupting agent studied in direct comparison to latrunculin A.
Capping of actin filaments blocks barbed-end growth and alters cellular function.
Free barbed filament ends are normally suppressed by cellular cappers that prevent barbed-end growth.
Site-directed actin filament assembly drives motility, explaining why actin capping collapses cell shape and density.

reflection.next_experiment: Phalloidin F-actin vs acetylated-tubulin co-stain across a replicated dose range with washout, plus cell-free actin barbed-end elongation assay versus tubulin polymerization assay with paclitaxel control to prove primary actin capping and secondary tubulin compaction.

## Reflection

Unblinded truth was cytochalasin B, an Actin disruptor; I twice concluded Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.62 then p=0.38 and was wrong. The central error was treating monotonic tub_mean brightening to z=+44.6 at 30uM (e3) with rho=+1.00 (e9) and multinucleation to z~+21 at 3uM (e8) as stabilizer-specific.

The actin signal was present from the start but I discounted it. The 30uM microscopist read was Actin disruptors with no distinct bundles (e4), low doses already showed cell_area z=-8.4 to -4.1 with multinucleation z=+8.4 to +3.4 (e2, e7), and act_mean also rose with rho=+1.00 to z=+37.3 (e11). That pattern fits actin filament capping and failed cytokinesis rather than stabilization, consistent with cytochalasin B as a microfilament-disrupting agent (PMID 8781335) acting by barbed-end capping (PMID 12686620, PMID 10340699), where loss of directed assembly collapses morphology (PMID 1608453).

I was misled by acquisition and weighting choices: only n=1 per dose over 4 wells, so dose-responses were four single wells; high-dose rounding/compaction inflated tub and actin texture (tub_glcm_contrast z=+44.1, act_glcm_contrast z=+67.5 in e3); and I over-weighted one bundle-like vision at 3uM (e15) over conflicting visions (e4, e19) and atlas neighbours that never supported stabilizers at 1uM and 3uM — Protein synthesis 8/10 (e13) and Epithelial 5/10 (e18). The review was correct that actin was not shown to be secondary.

What was right:
- e4 high-dose vision of Actin disruptors with no distinct bundles correctly flagged the true MoA
- e2/e7/e8 cell_area shrinkage with reduced density and rising frac_multinucleate_proxy captured cytokinesis failure from actin-ring disruption
- e11 act_mean rho=+1.00 to high z and e3 actin texture explosion showed actin was co-primary, not secondary
- e13/e14/e18 atlas neighbours (Protein synthesis 8/10, Cholesterol-lowering 5/10, Epithelial 5/10) correctly warned against stabilizers

What was wrong or missed:
- misread tub_mean rise to z=+44.6 (e3, e8, e9) as stabilization when actin-collapse compaction also brightens tubulin
- treated multinucleation (e2, e8, e10) as stabilizer/Aurora-specific and missed actin-cytokinesis failure
- upgraded single 3uM bundle-like vision (e15) and initial atlas 3/10 stabilizers (e5) to p=0.62 despite e4 contradiction and n=1/dose
- failed to resolve that tub_mean and act_mean both had rho=+1.00 (e9 vs e11), so specificity for stabilizers was never demonstrated

Proposed next experiment: Phalloidin F-actin vs acetylated-tubulin co-stain across a replicated dose range with washout, plus cell-free actin barbed-end elongation assay versus tubulin polymerization assay with paclitaxel control to prove primary actin capping and secondary tubulin compaction.
